tldr: An Oct 9 arXiv paper split multimodal document QA agents into role-specialized locate, judge and read tools over a knowledge-point index. Until Oct 27, no follow-up appeared in the feed.
whats_new: Two Oct 27 papers extend the thread: RouteDRAG learns to route and control agentic execution for multimodal document RAG, and DocXEval benchmarks explainability in document understanding models.
why_it_matters: Document-QA agents are moving from one generalist tool-using model toward routed, role-specific stages, and explainability is now being measured separately from accuracy.

status.detail: Three arXiv preprints, no production releases: agent architecture for multimodal document RAG is converging on routing, while explainability evaluation lags.

beats.headline: Role-specialized tool agents split locating from reading
beats.summary: Separates retrieval tools from reading tools instead of giving one model both.

beats.headline: RouteDRAG learns to route and control agentic execution
beats.summary: Targets questions that need combining pages, tables and figures.

beats.headline: DocXEval evaluates explainability of document models
beats.summary: Addresses the black-box obstacle to safe deployment of multimodal document models.

open_questions: Do RouteDRAG or the locate-judge-read agents publish code or benchmark numbers on a shared multimodal document QA set?
Does any production document-QA product adopt routed or role-specialized retrieval and reading stages?
Do later papers report DocXEval explainability scores for the agentic RAG systems in this thread?
take_for_builders: Keep retrieval and reading as separate, individually evaluable stages in document-QA pipelines, and wait for released code or shared benchmarks before replacing a working setup with these preprints.
